title: Use NASA HIP identifiers to crosswalk confirmed exoplanet hosts into the YEIS/HYG native star catalog

scope.subject: Observed-system identity bridge between NASA Exoplanet Archive and YEIS/HYG stars

research_summary: The native YEIS star renderer can pick HYG catalog indices directly, but the old MIT YEIS snapshot does not contain the project's NASA confirmed-exoplanet systems. Name-only matching is incomplete because HYG's compact names table indexes Proper/Bayer/Gliese/HIP while many NASA hosts are HD names. NASA pscomppars already exposes hip_name, hd_name and gaia_dr3_id. A live TAP research query over the same nearest-host selection showed 51 of 64 hosts have HIP identifiers, and every one of those 51 HIP values exactly matches the vendored YEIS/HYG binary. Reuse that stable HIP identity key: add host identifiers to the local NASA snapshot, propagate HIP to observed GalaxyMarker metadata, then resolve HIP to YEIS catalog index at runtime. Keep Gaia/HD as retained metadata/fallback, not a new full catalog dependency.

sources.finding: NASA Exoplanet Archive TAP is the existing authoritative confirmed-system source and supports selecting additional host identity columns without adding a runtime dependency.
Live TAP_SCHEMA inspection on 2026-11-22 confirmed pscomppars columns hip_name, hd_name, gaia_dr3_id and gaia_dr2_id. A matching query over the nearest snapshot hosts found 51/64 HIP values.
YEIS StarCatalog stores a Uint32 HIP identifier for every HYG binary record and supports exact HIP lookup, making HIP the direct identity join key.
HYG combines Hipparcos and other nearby-star identifiers; the vendored YEIS binary is an HYG-derived compact representation whose HIP field is preserved.

search_ladder.conclusion: The selected mother already has HYG/HIP identities, but its MIT snapshot does not include the general confirmed exoplanet catalog, so a catalog-level bridge is still needed.
YEIS StarCatalog already exposes the exact HIP array and therefore no new identity framework or crossmatch engine is needed.
NASA TAP already provides HIP/HD/Gaia host identifiers; reusing those fields is more reliable and smaller than fuzzy names or another external catalog.
The existing HYG-derived stars.bin preserves HIP per record, so the crosswalk can be an in-memory index over already-vendored data.

coverage_matrix.capability: exact identity for NASA hosts that exist in HYG
coverage_matrix.decision: HIP is already present on both sides; measured 51/51 exact matches make it the primary key.

coverage_matrix.capability: no new large catalog or preprocessing pipeline
coverage_matrix.decision: HIP crosswalk reuses existing NASA snapshot and existing 2.6 MB YEIS binary.
Hosts without HIP remain separate NASA observed markers; no confirmed system is dropped.

coverage_matrix.capability: native star picking can route to observed override
coverage_matrix.decision: Store resolved YEIS nativeId on observed markers when HIP matches so native StarPoints clicks can select the NASA override directly.

candidates.name: NASA hip_name -> YEIS/HYG StarCatalog.hips exact crosswalk
candidates.license: NASA data + existing HYG CC BY-SA derived catalog
candidates.reason: Direct exact join using identifiers already present in both reused datasets; empirical check matched every HIP-bearing nearby host in the snapshot.

candidates.name: Normalize NASA hostname and fuzzy-search YEIS Proper/Bayer/Gliese names
candidates.reason: Misses common HD-only NASA hosts and risks false positives; useful only as a last-resort display aid, not identity authority.

candidates.name: Add a Gaia DR3 identity catalog/crossmatch layer
candidates.reason: Would cover some HIP-less hosts but the current HYG binary has no Gaia identifier field, so it would require another catalog/index pipeline before yielding value for native picking.

candidates.name: Keep all NASA observed systems as a disconnected marker layer
candidates.reason: Preserves correctness but prevents native star picks from resolving directly to known observed systems and leaves duplicate representations where a HYG match exists.

decision.rationale: Make HIP the authoritative cross-catalog identity when available, retain HD/Gaia IDs as metadata, and leave HIP-less NASA hosts intact as independent observed markers. This maximizes native renderer integration without adding a new catalog or weakening observed-system correctness.

higher_level_tradeoffs.reason: Gaia is broader but requires a new identity index on the HYG side; measured HIP coverage already resolves most nearby observed hosts at a fraction of the integration and maintenance cost.

decision.fallback: If a future observed host lacks HIP but must be merged into native picking, add an explicit curated identity override or a dedicated Gaia crossmatch task; do not silently use fuzzy names as authority.
